question: The principle that "possession is prima facie proof of ownership" is provided under which section of the BSA, 2023?
explanation: Section 113 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 110 of the old Evidence Act) states that when the question is whether any person is owner of anything of which he is shown to be in possession, the burden of proving that he is not the owner is on the person who affirms that he is not the owner.

subject: BSA
question: The principle that 'possession is prima facie proof of ownership' is contained under Section.............of the BSA, 2023.
explanation: Section 113 embodies this rule.

subject: BSA
question: When the question is whether any person is the owner of anything of which he is shown to be in possession:-
options: the burden of proving that he is the owner is on the person who affirms he is not owner
the burden of proving that he is NOT the owner is on the person who affirms that he is not the owner
the burden of proving that he is owner lies upon him because he has established possession
explanation: Possession creates a statutory presumption of title; the burden to displace it lies on the person disputing ownership.

subject: BSA
question: Section 114 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 speaks of transactions where one person stands in a position of............to the other person.
explanation: Section 114 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 111 IEA) applies where one party stands in a position of 'active confidence' (fiduciary relation like lawyer-client, doctor-patient, parent-child).

subject: BSA
question: The good faith of a sale by a client to his advocate is in question in a suit brought by the client. Under Section 114 of the BSA, 2023:-
options: the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the advocate
the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the client
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 114 of the BSA, 2023: since the advocate stands in active confidence to the client, the burden of proving good faith is on the advocate.

subject: BSA
question: According to the BSA, 2023, which one among the following statements is NOT correct?
options: When shown a person was alive within 30 yrs, burden of proving him dead is on person who affirms it
When shown a person was not heard of for 7 yrs, burden of proving him alive is on person who affirms it
When shown a person is in possession, burden of proving he is not owner is on person who affirms he is not owner
When shown a person stands in active confidence, burden of proving good faith is on the party who reposed confidence
explanation: Statement D is incorrect because the burden of proving good faith lies on the party *in whom active confidence is reposed* (e.g. advocate/doctor), not on the party who reposed confidence. (The book answer key lists option D).

subject: BSA
question: In which group of sections of the BSA, 2023 is the burden of proof of NOT committing statutory offences (or presumption of guilt) placed on the accused?
explanation: Section 115 (presumption as to certain offences like terrorism/disturbed areas), 117 (abetment of suicide by married woman), 118 (dowry death), and 120 (absence of consent in rape) shift the burden onto the accused. (The book answer key lists option B).

subject: BSA
question: The statutory presumption as to the legitimacy of a child born during a valid marriage is provided under which section of the BSA, 2023?
explanation: Section 116 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 112 of the old Evidence Act) governs birth during marriage as conclusive proof of legitimacy.

subject: BSA
question: Section 116 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides for:-
explanation: Section 116 provides for presumption of legitimacy.

subject: BSA
question: If a child is born within............days after the dissolution of a valid marriage, the mother remaining unmarried, it is conclusive proof of the legitimacy of the child under Section 116 of the BSA, 2023.
explanation: Section 116 prescribes 280 days after dissolution.

subject: BSA
question: A child C was born after the dissolution of marriage between F and M. The legitimacy of child C will be taken as conclusive proof only if C was born within..........days after dissolution.
explanation: 280 days.

subject: BSA
question: In case a child is born within 280 days of the dissolution of marriage, the mother remaining unmarried, the presumption of legitimacy under Section 116 of the BSA, 2023 arises:-
options: If the father is alive on the day the child is born
If the father is not alive on the day the child is born
Irrespective of whether the father is alive or dead on the day the child is born
explanation: The statutory presumption under Section 116 operates purely on the 280-day timeline following dissolution, regardless of whether the former husband is alive or deceased when the child is born.

subject: BSA
question: Section 116 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 applies when there is a dispute regarding:-
explanation: Section 116 deals with who is the legal father (paternity) of a child born to a mother.

subject: BSA
question: Unless non-access is proved, the statutory presumption as to the legitimacy of any child born during the continuance of a valid marriage is classified as an:-
options: Mixed presumption of law and fact
explanation: Section 116 explicitly terms birth during valid marriage as 'conclusive proof' of legitimacy, which cannot be rebutted by any evidence other than proof of non-access.

subject: BSA
question: The presumption under Section 116 of the BSA, 2023 is raised:-
options: when a child is born during the continuance of a valid marriage
when a child is born within 280 days of dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried
explanation: Section 116 covers both limbs.

subject: BSA
question: Under the strict statutory wording of Section 116 of the BSA, 2023, the conclusive presumption of legitimacy can ONLY be rebutted by proving:-
options: that the parties to the marriage had no access to each other at any time when the child could have been begotten
the fact that wife was observing her menstrual period
the fact that the wife had undergone tubectomy
explanation: Section 116 states that birth during marriage shall be conclusive proof of legitimacy 'unless it can be shown that the parties to the marriage had no access to each other at any time when he could have been begotten'.

subject: BSA
question:
Evaluate the following legal statements:
A. The presumption under Section 116 of BSA, 2023 can be rebutted by a scientifically conclusive DNA Test.
B. *Falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus* is a mandatory rule of evidence in India.
options: A is correct and B is incorrect
A is incorrect and B is correct
explanation: In *Nandlal Wasudeo Badwaik v. Lata Badwaik*, the SC held that DNA test results outweigh the statutory presumption under Section 112 IEA. Statement B is incorrect because *falsus in uno* is not a rule of law in India. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BSA
question:
Assertion (A): Even for a child born immediately after marriage, the presumption of legitimacy under Section 116 of the BSA, 2023 would apply.
Reason (R): The Legislature which extended the operation of presumption by 280 days after dissolution did not choose to prescribe any minimum initial period of matrimony for the application of the presumption.
Select the correct code:-
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Even if a child is born one day after marriage, the statutory presumption applies because the law presumes marriage validates prior conception.

subject: BSA
question: Legitimacy of a child born during the continuance of a valid marriage under Section 116 of the BSA, 2023 is legally categorized as:-
explanation: Section 116 explicitly terms it 'conclusive proof'.

subject: BSA
question: Select the most appropriate statement regarding Section 116 of the BSA, 2023:
options: A child born during marriage is a conclusive proof of legitimacy
A child born during marriage may be presumed as a legitimate child
A child born during marriage shall be considered as conclusive proof of legitimacy unless rebutted by proof of non-access
No presumption will be drawn about a child born during marriage
explanation: Statement C captures the full statutory rule including the non-access exception.

subject: BSA
question:
Read the following statements carefully:
1. Presumption of legitimacy of child is governed by Section 116 of the BSA, 2023.
2. Narendra Nath Pahari v. Ram Govind Pahari is a leading case on the legitimacy of a child born during the continuance of a valid marriage.
From the above options:-
explanation: Both statements are correct under Indian law of evidence.

subject: BSA
question: The case of Ranatish Saha v. Smt. Soma Saha, AIR 2016 (NOC) 268 Cal, is related to which subject?
options: DNA Test for establishing non-access / legitimacy
Burden of proving fact especially within knowledge
explanation: *Ranatish Saha v. Soma Saha* (2016) dealt with ordering DNA tests to prove non-access under Section 112 IEA / Section 116 BSA. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BSA
question: In a criminal prosecution relating to the abetment of suicide by a married woman, the statutory presumption of abetment by husband/relatives is available in Section...........of the BSA, 2023.
explanation: Section 117 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 113A of the old Evidence Act) provides for presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman within 7 years of marriage.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 117 of the BSA, 2023 (abetment of suicide), the Court..............presume, and under Section 118 of the BSA, 2023 (dowry death), the Court..............presume.
explanation: Section 117 (Section 113A IEA) uses 'MAY presume', whereas Section 118 (Section 113B IEA - Dowry Death) uses 'SHALL presume'. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BSA
question: The presumption under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 pertains to:-
options: Abetment of suicide by a married woman
Absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape
explanation: Section 117 specifically governs presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman within 7 years of marriage.

subject: BSA
question: The Court will presume an abetment of suicide by a married woman under Section 117 of the BSA, 2023 when it is shown that she committed suicide within a period of.............of her marriage:
explanation: Under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 113A of the old Evidence Act), the statutory presumption of abetment of suicide arises if a married woman commits suicide within seven years of her marriage.

subject: BSA
question: For the presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman to arise under Section 117 of the BSA, 2023, it must be shown that:-
options: she committed suicide after 7 years of marriage
her husband and his relatives subjected her to cruelty
explanation: Section 117 requires proof that the suicide occurred within 7 years of marriage AND that her husband or his relatives subjected her to cruelty as defined in Section 85/86 of BNS, 2023.

subject: BSA
question:
In a case of suicide by a married woman, the court under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 may presume that the suicide was abetted by her husband if:-
1. Suicide was committed by the wife within seven years from the date of marriage.
2. The wife was subjected to cruelty.
3. The wife was illiterate and from a poor family.
4. The wife was deserted by the husband.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:-
explanation: The statutory pre-requisites under Section 117 are conditions (1) suicide within 7 years of marriage and (2) subjection to cruelty by husband or his relatives.

subject: BSA
question:
Evaluate the following legal statements under Section 117 of the BSA, 2023:
Statement A: The presumption under Section 117 of BSA, 2023 is not attracted if the marriage took place more than seven years prior to the suicide, even if cruelty is established.
Statement B: By the introduction of Section 117, the prosecution is not required to prove facts beyond reasonable doubt against the accused.
Which statement is correct?
explanation: Statement A is correct because the 7-year statutory period is an absolute prerequisite. Statement B is incorrect because the initial burden of proving cruelty and suicide beyond reasonable doubt remains on the prosecution.

subject: BSA
question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Section 117 of the BSA, 2023?
(A) The presumption would be attracted if the marriage took place more than 7 years prior to suicide, provided cruelty soon before death is established.
(B) Because Section 117 is attracted, the prosecution is not required to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
explanation: Both statements (A) and (B) are incorrect. Section 117 strictly requires suicide within 7 years of marriage, and does not dispense with the prosecution's burden of proving the foundational facts beyond reasonable doubt.

subject: BSA
question: Which significant principle of law was declared by the Supreme Court of India in Pawan Kumar v. State of Haryana, AIR 2001 SC 1324?
options: Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman
explanation: In *Pawan Kumar v. State of Haryana* (2001), the Supreme Court laid down detailed guidelines regarding the applicability of the presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman under Section 113A IEA (Section 117 BSA).

subject: BSA
question: What does Section 118 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deal with?
explanation: Section 118 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 113B of the old Evidence Act) governs the statutory presumption as to Dowry Death.

subject: BSA
question: Which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is related to the presumption as to dowry death?
explanation: Section 118 of the BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: The presumption as to dowry death has been provided in which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 118 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Where a woman commits suicide within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death, her husband or his relative subjected her to cruelty in connection with any demand for dowry, it is a case of:-
options: presumption of abetment of suicide by husband or relative
both presumption of dowry death as well as presumption of abetment of suicide
presumption of cruelty caused to her
explanation: When dowry harassment leads to suicide within 7 years, both Section 117 (abetment of suicide) and Section 118 (dowry death under Section 80 BNS) presumptions are attracted.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT a pre-requisite of the presumption as to dowry death under Section 118 of the BSA, 2023?
options: Victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or relatives
Victim had illicit relationship with other male person
Cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry
It was done within 7 years of the marriage
explanation: An alleged illicit relationship is completely irrelevant and is not a statutory prerequisite under Section 118.

subject: BSA
question: An accused charged under Sections 103 and 80 of the BNS, 2023 is acquitted of the offence under Section 103 (murder). The statutory presumption under Section 118 of the BSA, 2023 for Section 80 (dowry death) is:-
explanation: Acquittal of murder does not prevent Section 80 BNS dowry death conviction if the statutory presumption under Section 118 BSA stands unrebutted. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is NOT a precondition to raise an obligatory presumption ('shall presume') under Section 118 of the BSA, 2023?
options: The accused is being tried for the offence under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
The deceased woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relative
Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry
Such cruelty or harassment was soon before her death
explanation: Section 118 applies specifically to prosecutions for dowry death under Section 80 BNS, 2023 (old Section 304B IPC), not standalone trials under the Dowry Prohibition Act.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statutory provisions and subjects under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: Presumption as to dowry death — Section 117 BSA
Presumption as to documents thirty years old — Section 92 BSA
explanation: Option A is incorrectly matched: Presumption as to dowry death is provided under Section 118 BSA (Section 117 governs abetment of suicide).

subject: BSA
question: Section 119 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Court may presume existence of certain facts) provides for certain:-
explanation: Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 114 of the old Evidence Act) deals with discretionary presumptions of fact (*may presume*).

subject: BSA
question: Section 119 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides which of the following?
options: The Court may ask questions to parties
The Court may presume existence of certain facts
The Court may call upon extra proof
explanation: Section 119 empowers the Court to presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regarding human conduct and common course of business.

subject: BSA
question: 'A man is in possession of stolen goods soon after the theft.' Choose the correct presumption under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 which the Court MAY presume:-
options: That he is an innocent person
That he must be knowing the thief
That he is either the thief or has received the goods knowing them to be stolen
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 114 Illustration a): stolen goods possession soon after theft.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following presumptions under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 is NOT correct?
options: That an accomplice is unworthy of credit
That an accomplice is NOT unworthy of credit
That Judicial and Official Acts have been regularly performed
That a common course of business has been followed in particular cases
explanation: Under Illustration (b) to Section 119, the statutory presumption is that 'an accomplice is unworthy of credit, unless he is corroborated in material particulars'. Statement B is opposite and incorrect.

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following cases MAY the court presume facts under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023?
options: That a man in possession of stolen goods soon after theft is either thief or receiver
That judicial and official acts have been regularly performed
That evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavourable to the person withholding it
explanation: All three are statutory illustrations (a, e, g) to Section 119 of the BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023, the Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, having regard to:-
explanation: Section 119 specifies: 'having regard to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business'.

subject: BSA
question: Which illustration of Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 is based upon the legal maxim 'Omnia praesumuntur rite et solemniter esse acta' (all acts are presumed to have been done rightly and regularly)?
explanation: Illustration (e) to Section 119 ('that judicial and official acts have been regularly performed') is directly based on *omnia praesumuntur rite esse acta*.

subject: BSA
question: Section 119 Illustration (g) of the BSA, 2023 refers to the adverse inference presumption as to:-
explanation: Illustration (g) to Section 119 provides that evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavourable to the person withholding it (Adverse Inference).

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023, the Court MAY presume that:-
options: when a document creating an obligation is in the hands of the obligor, the obligation has been discharged
judicial and official acts have not been regularly performed
a bill of exchange accepted or endorsed was endorsed for deficient consideration
explanation: Illustration (i) to Section 119 provides that when a document creating an obligation is in the hands of the obligor, the obligation has been discharged.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following facts MAY the Court presume to exist under the law of evidence?
options: When a woman states in her evidence before the court that she did not consent for sex in rape prosecution
A priest will always speak truth
explanation: Under Section 120 of the BSA, 2023 (and Section 119), absence of consent in rape prosecution is statutory.

subject: BSA
question: A person is seen with same bank notes immediately after a bank robbery. The statutory presumption under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023 is that:-
options: he has received stolen money with required knowledge
explanation: Under Section 119 Illustration (a), possession of stolen notes immediately after robbery raises the presumption that he is either the thief or receiver of stolen property.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is NOT true under Section 119 of the BSA, 2023? A shopkeeper is found in possession of a marked stolen 100 rupee note which he cannot account for:-
options: The court will presume that he is a thief
The court will presume that he has received the currency knowing it to be stolen
Such presumption will not arise if he continually receives money in the course of his business
explanation: Under the Proviso to Illustration (a) of Section 119, if a shopkeeper receives marked notes in the ordinary course of business, the presumption of theft does NOT arise. Hence (D) is the correct option.

subject: BSA
question: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecutions of rape cases is raised under which section of the BSA, 2023?
options: Section 119 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 121 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Section 120 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 114A of the old Evidence Act) provides for presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape.

subject: BSA
question: In a prosecution for rape, where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the woman states in her evidence before the court that she did not consent:-
options: the court may presume that she did not consent
the court may regard her evidence as conclusive proof that she did not consent
the court may require further proof that she did not consent
the court shall presume that she did not consent
explanation: Section 120 of the BSA, 2023 uses mandatory language: 'the court *shall presume* that she did not consent'.

subject: BSA
question: Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is related to:-
options: Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman
Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a woman
Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecution for rape
explanation: Section 120 deals with presumption as to absence of consent in rape prosecutions.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 120 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, presumption deals with:-
options: Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman
Judicial and Official acts have been regularly performed
Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecution for rape
explanation: Presumption as to absence of consent in rape prosecution.

subject: BSA
question: In a case where a doctor commits rape on a woman of 30 years of age under his treatment and the woman says that she did not consent, the court:-
options: shall presume that she did not consent
may presume or may not presume her consent
explanation: Custodial/professional rape by medical personnel is covered under Section 120 BSA (old Section 114A IEA), so the court *shall presume* lack of consent.

subject: BSA
question: The statutory presumption under Section 120 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is a/an:-
options: mixed presumption of law and fact
explanation: Section 120 uses 'shall presume', which is a rebuttable presumption of law.

subject: BSA
question: Rules as to burden of proof are legally categorized as:-
explanation: Rules governing burden of proof are rebuttable presumptions of law.

subject: BSA
question: The burden of proof in judicial proceedings is lightened by:-
explanation: Presumptions, admissions, and rules of estoppel all operate to dispense with or lighten the evidentiary burden.

subject: BSA
question: In which Sections of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 are provisions of 'Estoppel' given under Chapter VIII?
explanation: Chapter VIII of the BSA, 2023 ('Estoppel') comprises Sections 121 to 123 (corresponding to Sections 115 to 117 of the old Evidence Act).

subject: BSA
question: Which section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deals with general principles of estoppel?
explanation: Section 121 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 115 IEA) contains the general rule of Estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Promissory estoppel is the extension of principle contained in which provision of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Promissory estoppel is an equitable doctrine developed by courts as an extension of Section 121 BSA (Section 115 IEA).

subject: BSA
question: The doctrine of estoppel fundamentally means:-
options: Not to make statement in consonance to the earlier statement
Restriction to make statement contrary to the earlier statement/admission
explanation: Estoppel is a rule of evidence which debars a person from denying or contradicting a representation previously made by him upon which another has acted.

subject: BSA
question: Section 121 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deals with:-
options: estoppel of acceptor of bill of exchange, bailee or licensee
evidence as to affairs of state
explanation: Section 121 defines general estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is NOT a recognized kind of estoppel?
explanation: The recognized legal categories of estoppel are Estoppel by Record, Estoppel by Deed, and Estoppel by Conduct (pais). 'Estoppel by Will' is not a recognized legal form of estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Estoppel can be created by:-
explanation: Estoppel may arise by active representation, recitals in formal deeds, attestation, or passive standing-by/acquiescence.

subject: BSA
question: The doctrine of Estoppel provided under Section 121 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 can be applicable:-
explanation: Estoppel can arise by representation, silence (where there is a duty to speak), gross negligence, or doctrine of election.

subject: BSA
question: A person cannot deny a statement previously made by him upon which another has acted. This principle is called:-
explanation: This is the classic definition of Estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' intentionally and falsely leads 'B' to believe that certain land belongs to 'A' and thereby induces 'B' to buy and pay for it. The land afterwards becomes the property of 'A', and 'A' seeks to set aside the sale on the ground that at the time of the sale he had no title. 'A' is not allowed to prove his want of title under Section...........of the BSA, 2023.
explanation: This is the verbatim Illustration to Section 121 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 115 Illustration).

subject: BSA
question: 'A' intentionally and falsely led 'B' to believe that a plot of land belonged to him. On that basis, he induced 'B' to buy and pay for it. Afterwards the plot of land became the property of 'A'. 'A' brought a suit to set aside the sale in favour of 'B' on the ground that, at the time of sale, he had no title. In such suit:-
options: 'A' may prove want of title at the time of sale
'A' cannot be allowed to prove want of his title
It depends on the value of the property
explanation: Under Section 121 of the BSA, 2023, 'A' is estopped from proving his lack of title at the time of sale.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' intentionally and falsely leads 'B' to believe that certain land belongs to 'A' and thereby induces 'B' to buy and pay for it. The land afterwards becomes the property of 'A'. 'A' must not be allowed to prove his want of title:-
options: Because of the principle of res-judicata
explanation: This rule is governed by the doctrine of Estoppel (Section 121 BSA).

subject: BSA
question: The principle which precludes a person from denying some statement previously made by him is known as:-
explanation: Estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following does NOT figure in Section 121 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 while dealing with applying the principle of Estoppel?
explanation: The exact statutory terms in Section 121 are 'declaration, act or omission'. The word 'conduct' does not explicitly figure in Section 121 text.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT in the context of 'Estoppel' as dealt with in Section 121 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
options: There must be a representation by a person to another
The representation must be in writing
The other person must have acted upon such representation taking it as true
The other person should have suffered some prejudice or detriment by acting upon such representation
explanation: Estoppel does NOT require the representation to be in writing; oral declarations, acts, or omissions are equally effective.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding Estoppel under Section 121 of the BSA, 2023?
options: Section 121 of BSA applies to contracts by infants
Pardanashin ladies are exempted from estoppel
A representation made by an agent is effectual for the purpose of estoppel as if it had been made by his principal
An admission by an advocate even if erroneous in law is binding on his client
explanation: An agent acting within the scope of his authority binds the principal by estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: The doctrine of estoppel is legally classified as a:-
explanation: Estoppel is a rule of evidence, not a cause of action or substantive law.

subject: BSA
question: Plea of Estoppel in civil litigation:-
options: May be specifically pleaded or may not be specifically pleaded
explanation: Estoppel is a mixed question of fact and law and must be specifically pleaded in pleadings.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT an exception to the doctrine of estoppel under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
options: When the truth is known to both the parties
explanation: Estoppel operates precisely on questions of fact. There is no estoppel against statute/law, or when truth is known to both parties.

subject: BSA
question: Mark the CORRECT statement regarding the application of Estoppel:
options: The doctrine of estoppel is applied only in civil matters
The doctrine of estoppel is applied only in criminal matters
The doctrine of estoppel is applied in civil and criminal matters
All the above statements are wrong
explanation: Estoppel is strictly a rule of civil jurisprudence and has no application in criminal trials.

subject: BSA
question: A news item in the newspaper stated that those who open industrial units in North-East India will be exempted from Corporate Tax for 5 years. 'X' applied to Director of Industries who confirmed the availability of exemption. 'X' proceeded with his plans. However, the State Government withdrew its policy after one year. Can 'X' bring estoppel against the State?
options: No, because estoppel cannot be against State
No, as there was no direct promise between the State and X
Yes, X can bring a suit of promissory estoppel as he suffered detriment on the promise
It will be at the discretion of Court
explanation: Provided in the source text answer key as option (a).

subject: BSA
question: Mr. 'X' managed to get admission in MBBS course under a false caste certificate. University took three long years in verifying it and ultimately cancelled admission of Mr. 'X'. Can estoppel work against the university?
options: Yes, as it took 3 years to cancel admission
No, as the student has committed fraud himself
No, as it is against the Statutes
Yes, as equity favours Mr. X
explanation: Fraud vitiates everything. A person who obtains admission by fraud cannot invoke estoppel against statutory university regulations. (The book answer key lists option B).

subject: BSA
question: Which to the following statements is NOT correct regarding Estoppel?
options: A rule of law cannot be nullified by resorting to doctrine of estoppel
Assurances held out but not incorporated in an agreement would not attract doctrine of estoppel
Plea of promissory estoppel shall be available even if an officer of the Government acts outside the scope of his authority
An estoppel arises as soon as the relationship of landlord and tenant is created and tenant is not permitted to deny the title of his landlord
explanation: Statement C is incorrect: Promissory estoppel CANNOT be invoked against an officer acting beyond his statutory authority.

subject: BSA
question: Which section of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 [Now, Section 121 of BSA, 2023] is founded upon the landmark doctrine laid down in Pickard v. Sears?
explanation: *Pickard v. Sears* (1837) is the landmark English decision by Lord Denman which formulated the doctrine of Estoppel by representation embodied in Section 115 IEA / Section 121 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following cases was the principle of estoppel clearly framed in English law?
options: Polanski v. Conde Nast Publications Ltd.
explanation: *Pickard v. Sears*.

subject: BSA
question: Section 115 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 [Now, Section 121 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023] is founded upon the doctrine laid down in which of the following cases?
options: B. Coleman v. P.P. Das Gupta
explanation: *Pickard v. Sears*.

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court raise doubts regarding the applicability of the doctrine of equitable estoppel beyond Section 115 IEA [Section 121 BSA]?
options: Mercantile Bank of India Ltd. v. Central Bank of India Ltd.
Turner Morrison and Co. v. Hungerford Investment Trust Ltd.
explanation: *Madanappa v. Chandramma* (1965) is the leading Supreme Court authority on estoppel by representation and acquiescence.

subject: BSA
question: The celebrated case of Sarat Chunder Dey v. Gopal Chunder Laha, (1891) 19 LA 203 is related to which section of evidence law?
explanation: *Sarat Chunder Dey v. Gopal Chunder Laha* (1892) is the Privy Council's locus classicus on Estoppel under Section 115 IEA / Section 121 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: The leading case Sarad Chandra Dey vs. Gopal Chandra Laha is related to which principle of evidence?
explanation: Estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT a case on Estoppel?
options: Palvinder Kaur v. State of Punjab
Sarat Chand Dev v. Gopal Chand Laha
explanation: *Palvinder Kaur v. State of Punjab* is a landmark case on Confessions, not Estoppel.

subject: BSA
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is a tenant of immovable property estopped from denying the title of the landlord to that property?
explanation: Section 122 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 116 of the old Evidence Act) governs estoppel of tenant and of licensee of person in possession.

subject: BSA
question: Section 122 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (tenant estoppel) is applicable to:-
explanation: Section 122 explicitly refers to 'tenant of immovable property'.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 122 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the tenant is estopped from denying the title of the landlord:-
options: During the continuance of the tenancy
explanation: Section 122 explicitly provides: 'No tenant of immovable property... shall, *during the continuance of the tenancy*, be permitted to deny that the landlord had a title to such immovable property'.

subject: BSA
question: Section 124 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is related to:-
explanation: Section 124 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 118 of the old Evidence Act) lays down the general rule regarding 'Who may testify' (Competency of Witnesses).

subject: BSA
question: Under which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is the provision as to WHO COULD BE A WITNESS found?
explanation: Section 124 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which provision stipulates that a person of unsound mind can be a competent witness?
explanation: The provision that a person of unsound mind is a competent witness (unless prevented by his lunacy from understanding questions) is in Section 124 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (not BNS).

subject: BSA
question: Who MAY NOT testify under Section 124 of the BSA, 2023?
options: A person of unsound mind who is unable to understand question and to give a rational answer
explanation: Under Explanation to Section 124, a lunatic is not incompetent to testify, unless he is prevented by his lunacy from understanding the questions put to him and giving rational answers.

subject: BSA
question: Who out of the following is NOT competent to become a witness?
options: A person of unsound mind who is not prevented by his unsoundness of mind from understanding the questions put to him and giving rationale answer
An Adult whose body and mind are not functioning
A Child who is sufficiently developed to answer
explanation: A person whose mind is not functioning is incapable of understanding questions or giving rational answers.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is NOT a competent witness?
explanation: A mentally retarded person who cannot understand questions or give rational answers is incompetent.

subject: BSA
question: Who amongst the following is NOT a competent witness under Section 124 of the BSA, 2023?
explanation: An idiot (person completely devoid of understanding from birth) is incapable of giving rational answers and is incompetent.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 124 of the BSA, 2023, all persons are competent to testify unless the court considers that they are prevented from understanding the questions put to them because of:-
explanation: Section 124 explicitly lists 'tender years, extreme old age, disease, whether of body or mind, or any other cause of the same kind'.

subject: BSA
question: Any person can become incompetent to testify on which of the following grounds?
options: Tender age and extreme old age
Disease whether of mind or body
Any one of the above grounds
explanation: Section 124 encompasses all these grounds.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT a competent witness to testify under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
options: Persons capable of understanding the questions put to them by the court
explanation: An idiot is legally incompetent as a witness.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is NOT a competent witness under Section 124 of the BSA, 2023?
options: A person unable to understanding the questions put to them or unable to giving rational answers to those questions
explanation: The sole statutory test of competency under Section 124 is the intellectual capacity to understand questions and give rational answers.

subject: BSA
question: Who amongst the following are competent witness?
explanation: Chance witnesses, rape victims, and related witnesses are all competent witnesses under Indian law.

subject: BSA
question: In which celebrated judgment did the Hon'ble Supreme Court classify witnesses into three categories: (i) wholly reliable, (ii) wholly unreliable, (iii) neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable?
options: Vadivelu Thevar Vs. State of Madras, AIR 1957 SC 614
Guli Chand & Ors. Vs. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1974 SC 276
Ramnaresh & Ors. Vs. State of Chhattisgarh, AIR 2012 SC 1357
Bheru Singh Vs. State of Rajasthan, (1994) 2 SCC 467
explanation: In *Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras* (1957), Justice B.P. Sinha classified witnesses into three categories and affirmed that conviction can be based on the uncorroborated testimony of a single wholly reliable witness.

subject: BSA
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 may a witness unable to communicate verbally give evidence in any other manner?
explanation: Section 125 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 119 of the old Evidence Act) governs evidence given by a witness unable to communicate verbally (dumb witness).

subject: BSA
question:
Who among the following is competent to adduce evidence under Section 125 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
1. Dumb witness
2. Deaf witness
Select the correct answer using the code given below:-
explanation: Under Section 125 BSA, a witness who is unable to speak (dumb or deaf) is fully competent to give evidence by writing or signs in open court.

subject: BSA
question: A witness unable to communicate verbally may give his evidence by writing or sign in open court; such evidence shall be deemed to be:-
options: It depends on the discretion of the court to accept it or not
explanation: Section 125 explicitly provides: 'and evidence so given shall be deemed to be *oral evidence*'.

subject: BSA
question: Evidence given by a witness, unable to communicate verbally in the Court by writing or sign, shall be deemed to be:-
explanation: Under Section 125 BSA, 2023, signs or writings by a dumb witness in open court are legally classified as oral evidence.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding a witness unable to communicate verbally?
options: A witness unable to communicate verbally may give evidence in any manner which can make it intelligible
A witness unable to communicate verbally may give his evidence by writing in open court
A witness unable to communicate verbally may give his evidence by signs in open court
Evidence given by a witness unable to communicate verbally in writing before the court shall be deemed to be documentary evidence
explanation: Statement D is incorrect because the statute explicitly mandates that such evidence shall be deemed to be *oral evidence*, NOT documentary evidence.

subject: BSA
question: Which option is NOT correct under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
options: Expert witness under Section 39 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Hostile witness under Section 157 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
A witness unable to communicate verbally under Section 126 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Child witness under Section 124 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Option C is incorrect because a witness unable to communicate verbally is governed by Section 125 BSA, 2023 (not Section 126).

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which among the following does NOT come under the category of privileged communications?
options: Communications made by a witness who is unable to communicate verbally
explanation: Evidence given by a dumb witness under Section 125 is public testimony in open court, not a privileged communication.

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 removes the bar of doctrine that 'husband and wife were one person' in law?
explanation: Section 126 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 120 of the old Evidence Act) explicitly provides that in all civil proceedings the parties to the suit, and the husband or wife of any party, shall be competent witnesses.

subject: BSA
question: Under which section is it provided that in all civil proceedings the husband or wife of any party to the suit shall be a competent witness?
explanation: Section 126 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: What is the evidentiary value of evidence given by husband against wife and vice versa under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
options: Both are considered one identity in law, therefore one cannot adduce evidence against the other
Evidence can be adduced only in criminal proceedings by both
Evidence can be adduced by both in civil and criminal proceedings
explanation: Under Section 126 of the BSA, 2023, husband and wife are competent witnesses for and against each other in both civil proceedings and criminal trials.

subject: BSA
question: Husband and wife both are competent witness for each other:-
explanation: Section 126 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: A document containing a communication from a husband to his wife in the hands of a third person is:-
options: not admissible in evidence until consented to by the writer of the communication
explanation: In *R. v. Rulis* / *S.J. Choudhary v. State*, the courts held that marital privilege under Section 122 IEA (Section 128 BSA) attaches to the spouse as a witness, but a written letter intercepted by or coming into the hands of a third party is admissible secondary evidence.

subject: BSA
question: A husband or wife are permitted to disclose any communication between them during marriage:-
options: In civil proceedings between the parties
In criminal proceedings between the parties
In matrimonial proceedings between the parties
explanation: Under Section 128 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 122 IEA), marital privilege does not apply in suits between married persons or in proceedings in which one married person is prosecuted for any crime committed against the other.

subject: BSA
question: In criminal proceedings against any person, the husband or wife of such person, shall be:-
options: Competent witness only if they are major and with the consent of other
Competent witness only if they are sane and with the consent of other
explanation: Section 126 of the BSA, 2023 explicitly states that in criminal proceedings against any person, the husband or wife of such person shall be a competent witness.

subject: BSA
question: As per Section 126 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which of the following has been stipulated?
options: Wife of a party is not a competent witness in a civil proceeding
Husband of a party is not a competent witness in a civil proceeding
Wife of an accused is not a competent witness in a criminal proceeding
explanation: Section 126 stipulates that husband and wife ARE competent witnesses in both civil and criminal proceedings, so statements A, B, and C are all false.

subject: BSA
question: Under which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a Judge cannot be compelled to answer any question as to his own conduct in court as such Judge?
explanation: Section 127 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 121 of the old Evidence Act) governs privilege of Judges and Magistrates.

subject: BSA
question: Section 127 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides for privileges in respect of which of the following?
explanation: Section 127 protects Judges and Magistrates from being compelled to answer questions regarding their judicial conduct.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 127 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, who among these has privilege?
options: Evidence in respect of affairs of the State
explanation: Judges and Magistrates.

subject: BSA
question: The judicial privilege under Section 127 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is:-
options: May or may not be available to an Arbitrator
explanation: Judicial privilege under Section 127 applies strictly to Judges and Magistrates, not to private Arbitrators. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BSA
question: A Magistrate can be compelled to answer questions on his own conduct as a Magistrate in Court ONLY:-
options: By an order of court to which he is subordinate
explanation: Under Section 127 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 121 of the old Evidence Act), a Judicial Officer cannot be compelled to answer questions regarding his judicial conduct except upon the special order of a Court to which he is subordinate.

subject: BSA
question: During the course of trial of a rape case, a person present in Court causes a knife injury to another person before the Court. The Judge before whom the incident took place:-
options: May not be called in evidence
May be called in evidence only under special order of a higher Court
May be examined as a witness
May be called in evidence only if trial of that incident is going on before a higher Court
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 127 of the BSA, 2023: a Judge may be examined as to matters which occurred in his presence while acting as Judge.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' is accused before the Court of Session of attempting to murder a Police Officer whilst on his trial before 'B', a Sessions Judge. In this case, whether 'B' may be examined?
options: B is protected by Section 130 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
B may be examined as to what occurred
explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 127 of the BSA, 2023: B may be examined as to what occurred in his presence.

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 protects from disclosing communication made during marriage?
explanation: Section 128 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 122 of the old Evidence Act) provides statutory privilege to marital communications.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 128 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, 'privilege' as to communications during marriage is available to:-
explanation: Marital privilege protects communications between a husband and wife.

subject: BSA
question: A communication made to a spouse during marriage, under Section 128 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:-
options: Remains privileged communication after the dissolution of marriage by divorce or death
Does not remain privileged after the dissolution of marriage by divorce or death
Does not remain privileged after divorce but remains privileged after death
Remains privileged after divorce but not so after death
explanation: The privilege attached to communications made during subsistence of marriage survives even after the marriage is dissolved by divorce or death of either spouse.

subject: BSA
question:
Assertion (A): 'S' writes to his wife 'C' a letter which contains defamatory matters about 'D'. 'C' cannot be compelled to disclose this communication.
Reason (R): Any communication made during subsistence of marriage by a husband to his wife or vice-versa is protected as privileged communication.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:-
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both Assertion and Reason are correct under Section 128 of the BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' and 'B' were married. During marriage 'A' committed forgery and communicated it to 'B', his wife. After some time divorce took place between 'A' and 'B', and 'B' married 'C'. In a charge against 'A' for forgery, the prosecution wants to produce 'B' as a witness against 'A'. Can they do so?
options: They can do so as B is now married to C
They can do so as forgery is an offence against public policy
They cannot do so as B is bound not to be witness against A under privileged communications
They cannot do so as B has now nothing in common with A and is a third party
explanation: Under Section 128 of the BSA, 2023, communications made during marriage remain privileged even after divorce, and B cannot be compelled or permitted to disclose them without A's consent.

subject: BSA
question: When can any communication made during marriage be permitted to be disclosed under Section 128 of the BSA, 2023?
options: in the civil proceeding between the husband and the wife
in the criminal proceedings instituted either by the wife or the husband against the other spouse
explanation: Section 128 explicitly permits disclosure in suits between married persons or proceedings for crimes committed by one against the other.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized privileged communication under Indian evidence law?
explanation: Paternal communication (father-child) is not recognized as a statutory privileged communication under the BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which among the following does NOT come under the category of privileged communications?
options: Communications made by a witness who is unable to communicate verbally
explanation: Dumb witness evidence under Section 125 is open court oral evidence, not a privileged communication.

subject: BSA
question: The privilege to withhold documents/information relating to Affairs of State under administrative law is enacted in which Section of the BSA, 2023?
explanation: Section 129 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 123 of the old Evidence Act) governs privilege as to evidence regarding Affairs of State.

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deals with evidence as to affairs of State?
explanation: Section 129 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is based on the legal maxim 'Salus populi est suprema lex' (welfare of the people is the paramount law)?
explanation: Section 129 (Affairs of State privilege) is based on the maxims *Salus populi est suprema lex* and *nam publici juris est regis*.

subject: BSA
question: Documents in respect of which privilege has been provided under Section 129 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 must be:-
explanation: Section 129 strictly applies to 'unpublished official records relating to any affairs of State'.

subject: BSA
question: Under which Section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a public servant shall not be compelled to disclose communications made to him in official confidence?
explanation: Section 130 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 124 of the old Evidence Act) governs privilege for Official Communications.

subject: BSA
question: For protection under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the communication is to be made:-
options: To a public officer in official confidence
To a public officer as an ordinary cause of his duties
To a public officer as a routine matter
explanation: Section 130 applies exclusively to 'communications made to him in official confidence'.

subject: BSA
question: A public officer under Section 130 of the BSA, 2023:-
options: cannot be compelled to disclose communications made to him in official confidence if he does not consider that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure
cannot be compelled to disclose communications made to him officially if he considers that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure
can be compelled to disclose communications made to him officially if he does not consider that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure
can be compelled to disclose communications made to him officially if he considers that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure
explanation: Section 130 states: 'No public officer shall be compelled to disclose communications made to him in official confidence, when he considers that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure.'

subject: BSA
question: No revenue officer shall be compelled to say whence he got any information as to the commission of any offence against the public revenue under:-
explanation: Section 131 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 125 of the old Evidence Act) protects Magistrates, Police officers, and Revenue officers from disclosing sources of information as to offences.

subject: BSA
question: Provision regarding professional communication (attorney-client privilege) is given under Section............of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
explanation: Section 132 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 126 of the old Evidence Act) governs Professional Communications.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 protects from disclosure of certain kinds of professional communications?
explanation: Section 132 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Communication by a client to an Advocate is not permitted to be disclosed under Section............of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
explanation: Section 132 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: 'A', a client says to 'B', an advocate – "I have committed forgery and I wish you to defend me." Under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is this communication protected?
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 132 of the BSA, 2023: a confession of past crime to an advocate for defence is protected under Section 132.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is an exception to Section 21 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Admissions)?
options: Section 132 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 165 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 131 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 155 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Professional communications under Section 132 constitute an exception to the admissibility of admissions.

subject: BSA
question: The protection of professional communication as provided under Section 132 to 134 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is available ONLY:-
options: for engaging an advocate to plead his case
for disclosing communication to advocate or his colleagues
before commission of the offence or illegal acts
after commission of the crime or illegal acts
explanation: Professional privilege under Section 132 protects communications made regarding past crimes for defence, but does NOT protect communications made in furtherance of future/ongoing illegal acts.

subject: BSA
question: 'Professional Communication' between Advocate and his client under Section 132 of the BSA, 2023:-
options: is a privilege communication only until the contract continues
is admissible in evidence with consent of the client
is not admissible until it is legal
explanation: Section 132 explicitly states that no advocate shall be permitted to disclose such communication *unless with his client's express consent*.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' a client says to 'B' an advocate – "I have committed forgery and I wish you to defend me". His communication is:-
options: Protected from disclosure because of Section 128 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Not protected from disclosure because of Section 128 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Protected from disclosure because of Section 132 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Not protected from disclosure because of Section 132 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Protected from disclosure under Section 132 Illustration (a).

subject: BSA
question: 'A', a client says to 'B', an advocate – "I have committed forgery and I wish you to defend me." Whether this is protected under professional communication?
explanation: Protected from disclosure under Section 132.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' being charged with embezzlement, retains 'B' an Advocate to defend him. In course of proceeding 'B' observes that an entry has been made in 'A's account, charging 'A' with sum said to have been embezzled, which entry was not in the book at the commencement of his employment. 'B' is:-
options: protected from disclosure under section 132 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
not protected from disclosure under section 132 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
protected from disclosure under section 134 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 being confidential communication with Legal Advisor
explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 132 of the BSA, 2023: a fact observed by an advocate showing that a fraud/crime has been committed since the commencement of his employment is NOT protected from disclosure.

subject: BSA
question: Legal Advisor:-
options: Can disclose the professional communication after death of his client
Can disclose the professional communication after the relationship with the client has ended
Can disclose professional communication if made in furtherance of any illegal purpose
Can disclose the professional communication in all the above instances
explanation: Under Proviso (1) to Section 132 of the BSA, 2023, communications made in furtherance of any illegal purpose are explicitly excepted from privilege.

subject: BSA
question: The professional communication between an advocate and his client can be disclosed before the court:-
options: With the consent of the client
Without the consent of the client if made in furtherance of any illegal purpose
Without the consent of the client if the advocate comes to know that any crime or fraud has been committed since the commencement of his employment
explanation: All three circumstances (express consent, illegal purpose proviso, or fraud committed during employment) allow disclosure.

subject: BSA
question: An accused informed his lawyer that he has committed the offence and wishes to defend him. In this circumstances:-
options: The lawyer is duty bound to inform the police about the information
The lawyer is duty bound to inform the fact to the Magistrate
The lawyer is not bound to disclose the communication which took place between him and the accused
The criminal court can compel the lawyer to disclose the fact
explanation: The communication is privileged under Section 132 Illustration (a).

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following facts is protected from disclosure in a court of law?
options: A, a client, says to B, an advocate "I have committed forgery and I wish you to defend me"
A, a client, says to B, an advocate "I wish to obtain possession of property by the use of a forged deed on which I request you to sue"

A, being charged with embezzlement, retains B, an advocate to defend him. In the course of the proceedings, B observes that an entry has been made in A's account book, charging A with the sum said to have been embezzled, which entry was not in the book at the commencement of his employment
A, a client says to his advocate B, "I want to murder my enemy C. Please advise me how I may be able to murder C"
explanation: Option A is protected under Section 132 Illustration (a). Options B, C, and D are statutory exceptions (illegal purpose / ongoing fraud).

subject: BSA
question: 'A' (a client) says to 'B' (an attorney): "I wish to obtain possession of property by use of a forged deed on which I request you to sue." According to Section 132 of the BSA, 2023, what is the legal position of this communication?
options: The communication is protected from disclosure
The communication is not protected from disclosure
explanation: This is Illustration (c) to Section 132 of the BSA, 2023: a communication made in furtherance of an illegal purpose (suing on a forged deed) is NOT protected from disclosure.

subject: BSA
question: 'A', a client, say to 'B', an advocate: "I wish to obtain possession of property by use of a forged deed on which I request you to sue."
options: This communication is protected from disclosure
This communication is not protected from disclosure
explanation: Not protected under Proviso (1) to Section 132.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
explanation: Professional communication is governed by Section 132 (not Section 130).

subject: BSA
question: Which one among the following is common in the provision of Section 129 and Section 132 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Privileged communications under Sections 129 and 132 are relevant to the matter in issue, but are rendered legally inadmissible due to statutory privilege.

subject: BSA
question: Section 134 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 states that no one shall be compelled to disclose to the Court any confidential communication which has taken place between:-
explanation: Section 134 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 129 of the old Evidence Act) protects confidential communications with legal advisors.

subject: BSA
question: Confidential communication with whom of the following is protected under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 134 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is a mismatch?
options: Confidential communication with legal advisor — Section 133
explanation: Option D is a mismatch: Confidential communication with legal advisor is governed by Section 134 of the BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides about the production of documents or electronic records which another person, having possession, could refuse to produce?
explanation: Section 136 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 131 of the old Evidence Act) governs production of documents or electronic records which another person having possession could refuse to produce.

subject: BSA
question: A witness cannot be converted into an accused person, though he may be compelled to answer questions relating to an offence. Under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, this immunity is granted to a witness?
explanation: Section 137 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 132 of the old Evidence Act) provides that a witness shall not be excused from answering on ground of self-incrimination, but Proviso to Section 137 grants immunity from arrest or prosecution based on such answers.

subject: BSA
question:
Assertion (A): Proviso to Section 137, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is a facet of rule against self-incrimination.
Reason (R): Policy of Section 137, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is to procure evidence for doing justice.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below:-
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both Assertion and Reason are true under Section 137 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: If question asked to a witness to any matter relevant to the matter in issue and the answer given by witness to such question will criminate him, then:-
options: The witness shall be compelled to answer such question
The witness shall not be compelled to answer such question
explanation: Under Section 137 of the BSA, 2023, a witness is compelled to answer relevant questions even if the answer criminates him (subject to statutory immunity).

subject: BSA
question: "An accomplice is a competent witness against an accused" is provided in which of the following Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 138 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 133 of the old Evidence Act) explicitly states: 'An accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused person'.

subject: BSA
question: An accomplice is a competent witness under:-
options: Section 124 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 125 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 137 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 138 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Section 138 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: An accomplice is a person who:-
options: participates in the commission of crime with the charged accused
explanation: An accomplice is a *particeps criminis* who consciously associates and participates in the commission of the crime with the accused.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is provided under Section 138 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 138 deals with Evidence of an Accomplice.

subject: BSA
question:
Assertion (A): The evidence of an accomplice requires to be accepted with a great degree of caution and scrutiny.
Reason (R): He hopes for pardon or has secured it and so favours the prosecution.
Code:-
options: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Provided in the source text answer key as option (b).

subject: BSA
question: Against whom shall an accomplice be a competent witness?
explanation: Section 138 states that an accomplice is a competent witness against an accused person.

subject: BSA
question: An accomplice:-
options: is not a competent witness against an accused person
is a competent witness against accused person
must be corroborated in that case
explanation: Section 138 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statement is correct with respect to an accomplice?
options: An accomplice shall not be a competent witness against an accused person
An accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused person
No conviction shall be made based on the uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice
An accomplice's testimony shall always be corroborated
explanation: Section 138 explicitly states that an accomplice is a competent witness, and conviction is not illegal merely because it proceeds upon uncorroborated testimony.

subject: BSA
question:
Assertion (A): An accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused person.
Reason (R): An accomplice is unworthy of credit, unless he is corroborated in material particulars.
Code:-
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Assertion A is Section 138 BSA (rule of law). Reason R is Illustration (b) to Section 119 BSA (rule of prudence). Both are true, but R is a rule of practice, not the legal explanation of competency.

subject: BSA
question:
Which of the following statement is/are not true?
(1) An accomplice is a competent witness against an accused person.
(2) Conviction on the testimony of an accomplice is legal.
(3) Conviction on the testimony of an accomplice is legal only if it is corroborated.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:-
explanation: Statement 3 is NOT true because as a matter of strict law (Section 138 BSA), uncorroborated conviction is not illegal, though prudence requires corroboration.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is correct statement according to law?
options: An accomplice shall be competent witness against an accused person
Leading question may be asked in cross-examination of a witness
The court may permit a party, who calls a witness, to put any question to him, which might be put in cross-examination by the adverse party
explanation: All three statements (Section 138, Section 146 leading questions, and Section 157 hostile witness) are correct provisions of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Who amongst the following is an accomplice?
options: A person giving bribe under coercion
explanation: A prostitute who participates in or facilitates an offence of immoral trafficking is considered an accomplice. Rape victims, trap witnesses, or coerced bribe givers are NOT accomplices.

subject: BSA
question: Who amongst the following is NOT an accomplice?
explanation: Detectives, police traps, or informers (*pretended confederates*) who join a conspiracy to detect crime without criminal intent are NOT accomplices.

subject: BSA
question: Mark the correct statement:-
options: an accomplice is unworthy of credit, unless he is corroborated in material particulars
an accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused, and conviction is not illegal merely because it proceeds upon uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice
None of the above is correct
explanation: Statement A is Illustration (b) to Section 119 BSA; Statement B is Section 138 BSA. Both read together form the complete legal position.

subject: BSA
question: Who among the following is NOT an accomplice?
options: An eye witness to a murder
explanation: Trap witnesses, victims of rape, and passive eyewitnesses to a murder are none of them accomplices.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about an accomplice?
options: Court may tender pardon to accomplice under Section 343 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Court may tender pardon only in those offences which are punishable up to 7 years of imprisonment
It is necessary for the court to record its reason in every case of pardon
The object of pardoning is to obtain evidence from the accused
explanation: Statement B is incorrect because pardon under Section 343 BNSS (Section 306 CrPC) can be tendered in offences punishable with imprisonment for 7 years or more or death/life imprisonment.

subject: BSA
question: Testimony of an accomplice before it is accepted and acted upon:-
options: must be corroborated from the testimony of another accomplice
must be corroborated from an independent source
need not be corroborated at all
need not be corroborated but corroboration is required as a rule of prudence
explanation: Corroboration of an accomplice's testimony is a rule of prudence (not an absolute mandate of law), and one accomplice cannot corroborate another accomplice.

subject: BSA
question:
An approver's evidence:-
1. must be reliable.
2. must be corroborated.
3. must be reliable and preferably corroborated.
4. is not admissible.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:-
explanation: An approver's evidence must pass the double test: it must be reliable as a witness and must be corroborated in material particulars.

subject: BSA
question: The landmark decision in Dagdu Vs. State of Maharashtra is related to:-
explanation: *Dagdu v. State of Maharashtra* (AIR 1977 SC 1579) is a leading Supreme Court case on accomplice evidence and the necessity of independent corroboration.

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following cases has the Supreme Court held that the testimony of a rape victim is NOT to be treated as that of an accomplice but as that of an injured person?
options: State of Rajasthan v. Narayan [AIR 1992 SC 2004]
Maqsoodan v. State of U.P. [AIR 1983 SC 126]
State of M.P. v. Dharkole [AIR 2005 SC 44]
State of U.P. v. Anil Singh [AIR 1988 SC 1998]
explanation: In *State of Rajasthan v. Narayan* (1992), the Supreme Court reiterated that a rape victim is an injured victim of crime and her testimony requires no corroboration like an accomplice.

subject: BSA
question: In criminal cases, when the confession of a co-accused is being tendered in evidence against another accused by the prosecution, and the other evidences on record fail to prove the prosecution, then the court should acquit such accused. In which case was it laid down so?
options: Haricharan Kurmi Vs. State of Bihar
explanation: In *Haricharan Kurmi v. State of Bihar* (1964), a 5-Judge Constitution Bench held that a co-accused's confession under Section 30 IEA (Section 24 BSA) is weak evidence and cannot be used as the starting point of proof.

subject: BSA
question: One of the most important principles of the law of evidence is that "evidence is to be weighed and not to be counted." This has been incorporated under which Section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 139 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 134 of the old Evidence Act) states: 'No particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any fact.'

subject: BSA
question: Which section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides that evidence shall be weighed not counted?
explanation: Section 139 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, how many witnesses are required for the proof of any fact?
explanation: Section 139 explicitly states that no particular number of witnesses is required.

subject: BSA
question: What minimum number of witnesses are required to prove offence of Dacoity in a trial?
options: Judge will direct how many witnesses are to be examined
No particular number of witnesses is prescribed for proving any fact
explanation: Under Section 139 BSA, even for grave offences like Dacoity, no specific number of witnesses is required; quality over quantity applies.

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, what number of witnesses will be required for the proof of any fact?
explanation: No particular number under Section 139.

subject: BSA
question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, how many number of witnesses are required to prove any fact?
explanation: No particular number required.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Minimum 2 witness are required for the proof of any fact.
Minimum 3 witness are required for the proof of any fact.
Minimum 4 witness are required for the proof of any fact.
No particular number of witnesses is required for proof of any fact.
explanation: Statement D is the exact statutory rule under Section 139 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: "At least two witnesses are required for proof of any fact under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023." Is this proposition true or false?
options: True. Deposition of a witness requires corroboration by another witness.
True. Chapter X of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 so requires.
True. Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 so requires.
False. Section 139 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 specifically mandates that there is no such requirement.
explanation: The proposition is false; Section 139 BSA explicitly mandates that no particular number of witnesses is required.

subject: BSA
question: In which celebrated judgment did the Hon'ble Supreme Court classify witnesses into three categories (wholly reliable, wholly unreliable, neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable)?
options: AIR 1957 SC 614, Vadivelu Thevar Vs. State of Madras
AIR 1974 SC 276, Guli Chand & Ors. Vs. State of Rajasthan
AIR 2012 SC 1357, Ramnaresh & Ors. Vs. State of Chhattisgarh
(1994) 2 SCC 467, Bheru Singh Vs. State of Rajasthan
explanation: *Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras* (1957) is the landmark judgment affirming that conviction can be based on the sole testimony of a single wholly reliable witness.

subject: BSA
question: The Order of production and examination of witnesses in Civil Suits under Section 140 of the BSA, 2023 is:-
options: First the plaintiff then the defendant
First the defendant and then the plaintiff
At the discretion of the parties
explanation: Section 140 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 135 of the old Evidence Act) states that the order of production and examination shall be regulated by the law and practice relating to civil and criminal procedure (CPC & BNSS).

subject: BSA
question: Which section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides that the Judge will decide as to admissibility of evidence?
explanation: Section 141 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 136 of the old Evidence Act) empowers the Judge to decide as to the admissibility of evidence.

subject: BSA
question: Admissibility of evidence is to be decided by:-
explanation: Under Section 141 BSA, the Judge alone decides admissibility.

subject: BSA
question: It is proposed to prove a fact (A) which is said to have been the cause or effect of a fact in issue. There are several intermediate facts (B, C and D) which must be shown to exist before the fact (A) can be regarded as the cause or effect of the fact in issue:-
