options: court will insist upon to first prove the fact (A)
court will insist upon to first prove B, C or D
the Court may either permit A to be proved before B, C or D is proved, or may require proof of B, C and D before permitting proof of A
the Court will not permit A to be proved before B, C or D is proved and may not require proof of B, C and D before permitting proof of A
explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 141 of the BSA, 2023: the Judge has discretion to allow proof of dependent facts in any order.

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 explains the meaning of "Examination-in-chief", "Cross-examination" and "Re-examination"?
explanation: Section 142 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 137 of the old Evidence Act) defines Examination-in-chief, Cross-examination, and Re-examination.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following kind of the examination of witness is provided under Section 142 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 142 defines all three kinds of examination.

subject: BSA
question: What is "Examination-in-chief"?
options: The examination of a witness by the party who calls him
The examination of a witness by the adverse party
The examination of a witness by the Magistrate
The examination of a witness after the cross-examination
explanation: Section 142 defines Examination-in-chief as the examination of a witness by the party who calls him.

subject: BSA
question: Examination-in-chief means:-
options: examination of a witness by adverse party
examination of a witness by Chief Judicial Magistrate
examination of a witness by Chief Superintendent of Police
examination of a witness by the party who calls him
explanation: Examination by the party who calls the witness.

subject: BSA
question: Cross-examination under Section 142 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 means which one of the following?
options: Examination of a witness by a party who calls him
Examination of a witness by the adverse party
Examination of a witness by a party who calls him and the adverse party
Examination of a witness by the Court
explanation: Section 142 defines Cross-examination as the examination of a witness by the adverse party.

subject: BSA
question: Right to cross-examine a witness is available to:-
explanation: Cross-examination is the exclusive right of the adverse party.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the questions is NOT lawful in cross-examination?
options: A question to test the veracity of the witness
A question to discover what the position in life of the witness is
A question the answer of which amounts to hearsay
A question to injure the character of the witness
explanation: Hearsay questions are inadmissible in evidence. Options A, B, and D are expressly permitted under Section 148 BSA (old Section 146 IEA).

subject: BSA
question: The object of cross-examination is:-
options: to examine the intelligence of the witness
to examine the impartiality of the witness
to examine the credibility of the witness
to examine the good character of the witness
explanation: The primary objective of cross-examination is to test the credibility, accuracy, and veracity of the witness's testimony.

subject: BSA
question: What are the questions which are lawful in cross-examination?
options: To take his credit by injuring the character
explanation: Section 148 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 146 IEA) permits all three categories of questions during cross-examination.

subject: BSA
question: What is re-examination of a witness?
options: Cross examination of one's own witness
Re-examination of a witness by the party who called him
explanation: Section 142 defines Re-examination as the examination of a witness, subsequent to cross-examination, by the party who called him.

subject: BSA
question: Re-examination of witness:-
options: can be for the purpose of filling what is left-over in examination-in-chief
can be for the purpose of explaining the matters referred to in cross-examination
can be for the purpose of explaining the matter referred to in examination-in-chief
explanation: Under Section 143 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 138 IEA), re-examination shall be directed to the explanation of matters referred to in cross-examination.

subject: BSA
question: The examination, after the cross-examination of a witness by the party who has called him, is called:-
explanation: Section 142 defines this as Re-examination.

subject: BSA
question: During re-examination of a witness:-
options: a new matter can be introduced as a matter of right generally
a new matter can be introduced only with the permission of the court
no new matter can be introduced at all
explanation: Under Section 143 of the BSA, 2023, if new matter is, by permission of the Court, introduced in re-examination, the adverse party may further cross-examine upon that matter.

subject: BSA
question: After re-examination of a witness, the adverse party has a:-
options: right to further cross-examine the witness afresh in general
has no right to further cross-examine the witness
right to further cross-examine the witness only when a new fact is introduced in the re-examination
explanation: The adverse party has a right to re-cross-examine only if new matter was introduced during re-examination with court permission under Section 143.

subject: BSA
question: To an answer to a court question, the adverse party:-
options: has a right to cross-examination as a matter of right
has a right to cross-examine only with the permission of the court
has no right to cross-examine the witness
explanation: Under Section 168 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 165 of the old Evidence Act), the parties cannot cross-examine any witness upon any answer given to a court question without the permission of the Court.

subject: BSA
question: When shall the witness be re-examined?
options: at the desire of adverse party
at the desire of party calling him
at the desire of the Magistrate
at the desire of the Police Officer
explanation: Re-examination is conducted by the party who originally called the witness.

subject: BSA
question: Re-examination of a witness:-
options: Can be for the purpose of filling what is left-over in examination-in-chief
Can be for purpose of explaining the matters referred to in cross examination
Can be for the purposes of explaining the matters referred to in examination-in-chief
explanation: Re-examination is strictly directed to explaining matters brought out during cross-examination.

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following judgements delivered by the Supreme Court in 2015, it was held that "it is imperative if the examination-in-chief is over, the cross-examination should be completed on the same day"?
options: Vinod Kumar v. State of Punjab
Ahmad Shah v. State of Rajasthan
Jasmer Singh v. State of Haryana
Inder Singh v. State of Rajasthan
explanation: In *Vinod Kumar v. State of Punjab* (2015), the Supreme Court expressed strong disapproval of delaying cross-examination after examination-in-chief and held that cross-examination must ideally be completed on the same day.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, Cross-examination of a witness:-
options: Must relate to relevant facts and has to be confined to what the witness testified in examination in chief
Must relate to relevant facts but need not be confined to what the witness testified in examination-in-chief
May not relate to relevant facts but must relate to what the witness testified in examination-in-chief
May not relate to relevant facts and may not be confined to what the witness testified in examination in chief
explanation: Under Section 143 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 138 IEA), cross-examination must relate to relevant facts, but need NOT be confined to the facts to which the witness testified in his examination-in-chief.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is true regarding further cross-examination?
options: There cannot be further cross-examination after re-examination
There can be further cross-examination after re-examination as per Section 142
There can be further cross-examination after re-examination as per Section 143
There can be further cross-examination after re-examination as per Section 144
explanation: Under Section 143 of the BSA, 2023, if new matter is introduced in re-examination with court permission, the adverse party may further cross-examine upon that matter.

subject: BSA
question:
Consider the following events and arrange them into correct chronological order:-
I. Cross examination
II. Examination in chief
III. Re-examination
Select the correct answer using the code given below:-
explanation: Under Section 143 of the BSA, 2023, witnesses shall be first examined-in-chief, then (if adverse party so desires) cross-examined, then (if party calling him so desires) re-examined.

subject: BSA
question: Which is the correct order of examination of witnesses?
explanation: Examination-in-chief → Cross-examination → Re-examination.

subject: BSA
question: A person summoned to produce a document when produces the document then:-
options: He cross-examined by both the parties
He is cross-examined with the permission of the court
He does not become witness and cannot be cross-examined unless and until he is called as a witness
explanation: Under Section 144 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 139 of the old Evidence Act), a person summoned to produce a document does not become a witness by the mere fact that he produces it, and cannot be cross-examined unless called as a witness.

subject: BSA
question: What is NOT true regarding examination of witnesses?
options: Witness may be cross-examined as to previous statement in writing
Leading question may be asked in cross-examination
Person called to produce document can be cross-examined
Party calling the witness may cross-examine him with the permission of Court
explanation: Option C is NOT true because under Section 144 BSA, a person merely called to produce a document cannot be cross-examined unless called as a witness.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following sections of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 contains provisions regarding cross-examination of witnesses to character?
explanation: Section 145 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 140 of the old Evidence Act) provides that witnesses to character may be cross-examined and re-examined.

subject: BSA
question: Which statement is INCORRECT regarding cross-examination?
options: In cross examination a witness may be asked questions which tend to discover what is his position in life
In cross examination a witness may be asked question which tend to test his veracity
Witnesses to character shall not be re-examined
In cross examination a witness may be asked question which tend to discover who he is
explanation: Option C is incorrect because under Section 145 of the BSA, 2023, witnesses to character MAY be re-examined.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is a CORRECT statement relating to cross-examination?
options: Witnesses to character may be cross-examined
Leading questions cannot be asked in cross-examination
A person summoned to produce a document can be cross-examined
A witness may not be cross-examined as to previous statements made by him in writing
explanation: Option A is correct under Section 145 BSA. Options B, C, and D are contrary to Sections 146, 144, and 148.

subject: BSA
question: "Leading question" has been defined in Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 under:-
explanation: Section 146 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 141 of the old Evidence Act) defines a Leading Question.

subject: BSA
question: As per Section 146 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 a "Leading question" means:-
explanation: Section 146 defines: 'Any question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive is called a leading question.'

subject: BSA
question: What do you understand by the term "Leading Question"?
options: Question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive
A question asked to contradict the witness by his previous writing
A question asked with reasonable ground
A question asked with a view to check the veracity of the witness
explanation: Section 146 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Any question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive is called:-
explanation: Leading question under Section 146.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is a leading question?
options: What did you see on the day of the incident?
How did you reach the spot of the incident?
Ajay confessed to you that he killed Pankaj?
What time did you leave home on 01st January?
explanation: Option C directly suggests the answer expected by the examiner, making it a leading question.

subject: BSA
question: Leading questions MAY be asked in examination-in-chief:-
options: with permission of the court as to matters which are introductory
If in the opinion of the court the matter involved has been already sufficiently proved
explanation: Under Section 146 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 142 IEA), the Court shall permit leading questions as to matters which are introductory or undisputed, or which have in its opinion been already sufficiently proved.

subject: BSA
question: During examination-in-chief or re-examination:-
options: Leading questions cannot be asked under any circumstances
Leading questions on certain matters can be asked without the permission of the court, as a matter of right
Leading question on certain matter can be asked only with the permission of the court
explanation: Under Section 146 of the BSA, 2023, leading questions must not, if objected to by the adverse party, be asked in an examination-in-chief, or in a re-examination, except with the permission of the Court.

subject: BSA
question: Under which of the following conditions, a leading question MAY be asked during examination-in-chief with the permission of the Court?
options: In matters which are disputed or not introductory
When matter in question is sufficiently proved
Under both of the above conditions
Under none of the above conditions
explanation: Section 146 explicitly permits leading questions in chief/re-examination as to matters which are introductory, undisputed, or sufficiently proved.

subject: BSA
question: What type of leading question MAY be asked in examination in chief with the permission of the court?
explanation: Introductory matters and already sufficiently proved matters.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 146 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, leading questions as to which matters can be permitted to be asked in examination-in-chief?
options: matters pertaining to character of a witness
explanation: Undisputed matters.

subject: BSA
question: Documents which are meant for cross-examination of a witness of the opposite party or meant for refreshing the memory of the witness may be produced:-
options: at or before the settlement of issues
at any time when they are required
explanation: Documents used during cross-examination or for refreshing memory can be produced at any time during cross-examination when required.

subject: BSA
question: Leading questions CAN be asked during:-
explanation: Under Section 146 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 143 IEA), leading questions MAY be asked in cross-examination as a matter of right.

subject: BSA
question: When can leading questions be asked?
options: In examination in chief with the permission of the court
In re-examination with the permission of the court
explanation: Leading questions can be asked in cross-examination (as of right) and in chief/re-examination (with court permission).

subject: BSA
question: A leading question, without the permission of the Court, may be asked in:-
explanation: Cross-examination.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Leading questions may be freely asked in examination-in-chief of a witness
Leading questions may be freely asked in cross-examination
Leading questions may be freely asked in re-examination
Leading question may not be put to a witness of tender years
explanation: Statement B is correct under Section 146 BSA.

subject: BSA
question:
Evaluate the following statements regarding leading questions:
A. In cross-examination.
B. In examination-in-chief, without permission of the Court.
Choose the correct option:-
options: A is correct and B is incorrect
A is incorrect and B is correct
explanation: Statement A is correct (leading questions permitted in cross). Statement B is incorrect (permission required in chief).

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 148 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a witness may be contradicted as to his previous statement in writing:-
options: without drawing his attention to the previous writing
after drawing his attention to the previous writing
without drawing or after drawing his attention to the previous writing
explanation: Under Section 148 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 145 of the old Evidence Act), if it is intended to contradict a witness by the writing, his attention must, before the writing can be proved, be called to those parts of it which are to be used for the purpose of contradicting him.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 148 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a witness MAY be cross examined as to previous statement in writing:-
options: after proving the same and showing the same to the witness
without proving the same but only after showing the same to the witness
after proving the same and reading the same to the witness
without proving the same and without showing the same to the witness
explanation: Under the first part of Section 148, a witness may be cross-examined as to previous statements in writing without such writing being proved or shown to him; but for *contradiction*, his attention must be drawn.

subject: BSA
question: A statement recorded by Investigation Officer under Section 180 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 161 CrPC) can be used:-
options: to refresh the memory of a witness
explanation: Under Section 183 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 162 CrPC), police statements can be used ONLY for contradicting the prosecution witness under Section 148 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: If a witness is intended to be contradicted during cross examination by his previous statement in writing, the same can be done:-
options: without such writing being shown to him
after his attention is called to those parts of the statement, which are used for the purpose of contradicting him
the previous writing of the witness can not be contradicted at all
explanation: Section 148 BSA mandatory procedure for contradiction.

subject: BSA
question: If a witness is intended to be contradicted during cross examination by his previous statement in writing, the same can be done:-
options: without such writing being shown to him
his attention must, before the writing can be proved, be called to those parts of its which are to be used for the purpose of contradicting him
the previous written statement of the witness can not be contradicted at all
explanation: His attention must be called to those parts used for contradiction.

subject: BSA
question: In prosecution for an offence under Section 64 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (rape), where the question of consent is an issue, it shall NOT be permissible to adduce evidence or put questions in cross examination of the victim as to general immoral character or previous sexual experience under Section.............of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
explanation: Section 149 Proviso of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 146 Proviso of the old Evidence Act) explicitly prohibits questioning the rape victim regarding her general immoral character or previous sexual experience.

subject: BSA
question: Questions unrelated to the subject matter of dispute and beyond examination in chief can be put to the witness:-
options: to test his veracity and shake his credit
discover who he is and what is his position in life
explanation: Under Section 149 of the BSA, 2023 (old Section 146 IEA), questions may be put in cross-examination to test veracity, discover position in life, or shake credit.

subject: BSA
question: Under Section 149 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which kind of questions CANNOT be asked during cross examination?
options: To test the veracity of witness
To discover the witness's position in life
Previous sexual experience of victims of offence of rape
explanation: Proviso to Section 149 prohibits questions regarding previous sexual experience of rape victims.

subject: BSA
question: In a prosecution for rape, questions in Chief-Examination of the prosecutrix as to her general immoral character are:-
options: permissible with the special permission of the court
permissible if the prosecutrix consents to it
explanation: General immoral character of the prosecutrix is completely impermissible and irrelevant under Section 149 Proviso & Section 51 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: For deciding whether or not a witness shall be compelled to answer questions, the court shall have regard to considerations which include as to whether such questions are:-
options: proper if the truth of imputation conveyed thereby would seriously affect the opinion of the court as to the credibility of the witness on the subject matter of his deposition
improper if the truth of imputation conveyed thereby would affect in a slight degree the opinion of the court as to the credibility of the witness on the subject of his deposition
explanation: Under Section 151 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 148 of the old Evidence Act), questions affecting credit are proper if truth of imputation seriously affects credibility, and improper if it affects credibility in a slight degree.

subject: BSA
question: The Judge's power to put questions or order production of documents does NOT include authorization to:-
options: compel a witness to answer any question which such witness is entitled to refuse to answer if the question were asked by the adverse party
to ask a question which would be proper for any other person to ask
to elicit clarity on a point
explanation: Under Proviso to Section 168 of the BSA, 2023 (Section 165 IEA), the Judge's power does not authorize compelling answers to privileged questions.

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 questions relating to a matter not relevant to the suit or proceedings MAY be asked under:-
explanation: Section 151 BSA governs questions testing credit on matters not otherwise relevant.

subject: BSA
question: "An advocate is instructed by another advocate that an important witness is a dacoit. This is a reasonable ground for asking the witness whether he is a dacoit." This illustration is based on which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 152 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 149 of the old Evidence Act: question not to be asked without reasonable grounds).

subject: BSA
question: In which of the following circumstances are there NO reasonable grounds for putting the question to the witness?
options: A, a barrister, is told by a solicitor that an important witness is a dacoit. The barrister asks the question "Are you a dacoit?"

An advocate is informed by a person in court that an important witness is a dacoit. The informant on being questioned by the advocate gives satisfactory reasons for his statement. The advocate asks this question, "Are you a dacoit?"
A witness of whom nothing whatever is known is asked at random whether he is a dacoit
A witness of whom nothing whatever is known on being questioned as to his mode of life and means of living gives unsatisfactory answers. The witness is asked, "Are you a dacoit?"
explanation: This is Illustration (c) to Section 152 of the BSA, 2023: asking an injurious question at random without any ground is prohibited.

subject: BSA
question: Indecent and scandalous questions may be forbidden by the court under:-
explanation: Section 154 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 151 of the old Evidence Act) empowers the Court to forbid indecent and scandalous questions.

subject: BSA
question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 the court MAY permit such questions which it regards indecent or scandalous if:-
options: they relate to facts in issue
they relate to the character of the accused
explanation: Section 154 states that the Court may forbid indecent or scandalous questions *unless they relate to facts in issue, or to matters necessary to be known in order to determine whether or not the facts in issue existed*.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
options: Burden of proof as to particular fact – Section 109, BSA, 2023
Indecent and scandalous question – Section 154, BSA, 2023
Confidential communication with legal advisor – Section 129, BSA, 2023
Questions intended to insult or annoy – Section 158, BSA, 2023
explanation: Option B is correctly matched: Indecent and scandalous questions are governed by Section 154 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which of the following is correctly matched?
explanation: Option C is correctly matched: Scandalous questions are under Section 154 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following questions shall NOT be asked in examining a witness?
options: only that which is intended to insult
only that which is intended to annoy
only that which appears to the Court needlessly offensive
explanation: Section 155 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 152 of the old Evidence Act) forbids questions intended to insult or annoy or needlessly offensive.

subject: BSA
question: According to Section 155 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the Court SHALL forbid any question which appears to it to be:-
options: to shake the credibility of a witness
explanation: Section 155 explicitly mandates forbidding questions intended to insult or annoy.

subject: BSA
question: Question intended to insult or annoy may be asked to a witness during:-
explanation: Questions intended to insult or annoy are forbidden at ALL stages of examination.

subject: BSA
question: 'A' affirms that on certain day, he saw 'B' at Goa. 'A' is asked whether he himself was not on that day at Varanasi. He denies it. Evidence is offered to show that 'A' was on that day at Varanasi.
options: the evidence is admissible as not contradicting the alleged fact that 'B' was seen on the day in question in Goa
The evidence is admissible as contradicting 'A' on a fact which affects his credit
The evidence is admissible, not as contradicting 'A' on a fact which affects his credit, but as contradicting the alleged fact that 'B' was seen on the day in question in Goa
explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 156 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 153 of the old Evidence Act: exclusion of evidence to contradict answers to questions testing veracity).

subject: BSA
question: The provision relating to "hostile witness" is provided under which of the following section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 157 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 154 of the old Evidence Act) governs Hostile Witness (question by party to his own witness).

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 the statement of hostile witness:-
explanation: It is settled law that the testimony of a hostile witness is not washed off the record entirely; those parts which support the prosecution or defense can be acted upon.

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, evidence of 'hostile witness':-
options: Cannot be taken into consideration for any purpose
It cannot be relied on by the prosecution
It can be relied only by the defence
It can be relied on by the prosecution as well as the defence
explanation: Evidence of a hostile witness can be relied upon by both prosecution and defense to the extent it is corroborated.

subject: BSA
question: A party can ask questions to his own witness under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 157 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: During examination-in-chief of a case under Section 117(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the victim denies the prosecution case. Under what provision of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the victim may be asked leading questions by the Public Prosecutor?
explanation: Under Section 157 of the BSA, 2023, when a prosecution witness resiles, the prosecutor can seek court permission to cross-examine / ask leading questions.

subject: BSA
question: Under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, prosecution or complainant MAY:-
options: not refresh memory of his witness
ask leading question to his own witness with the permission of the Court
ask leading question to his own witness without the permission of the Court
explanation: With court permission under Section 157 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: When can prosecution be allowed to ask leading question to its own witness?
options: When the witness is declared hostile
explanation: When the witness is declared hostile and court permission is granted under Section 157.

subject: BSA
question: Testimony of 'Hostile Witness' is to be:-
options: considered with caution and be corroborated
explanation: Hostile witness testimony is considered with caution and acted upon to the extent corroborated.

subject: BSA
question: Hostile witness means:-
options: A witness who is desirous of telling the truth
A witness who is not desirous of telling the truth
explanation: A hostile witness is an unfavourable witness who shows a mind hostile to the party calling him and conceals the truth.

subject: BSA
question: What option is available to a Commissioner when a party seeks permission to cross-examine his own witness?
options: He can permit the party to do so
He cannot permit the party to do so
He may ask the party to first obtain permission from Court under Section 157 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
He can permit the party to do so with the consent of the opposite party
explanation: A Commissioner appointed to record evidence cannot grant leave under Section 157; the party must obtain leave from the Court.

subject: BSA
question: Cross-examination of one's own witness is:-
options: permissible only after obtaining the permission of the court
permissible with the consent of the opposite party
explanation: Cross-examination of one's own witness under Section 157 BSA is permissible only with court permission.

subject: BSA
question: Party calling a person as witness CAN examine him:-
explanation: With permission of court under Section 157 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: A party who calls a witness:-
options: Can put any question to him which might be put in cross examination by the adverse party
Can put any question to him which might be put in cross examination by the opposite party only with the permission of the Court
Cannot put any question to him which might be put in cross examination by the opposite party even with the permission of the Court
Can in no case put a question to his own witness which might be put in cross examination by adverse party
explanation: Section 157 BSA allows putting cross-examination questions to one's own witness with court permission.

subject: BSA
question: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
options: Section 118 – Presumption as to dowry death
explanation: Option D is incorrectly matched: Section 157 governs Hostile Witness (Impeaching credit of witness is governed by Section 158 BSA).

subject: BSA
question: In which judgment Supreme Court held that "it hardly needs to be emphasised that one of the main reasons for witnesses to turn hostile is that they are not accorded appropriate protection by the state"?
options: Aashis Jain vs Makrand Singh and others (2019) 3 SCC 770
Pattu Rajan vs State of Tamil Nadu (2019) 4 SCC 771
Vinod Natesan vs State of Kerala and others (2019) 2 SCC 401
Mahender Chawla and others vs Union of India and others (2019) 14 SCC 615
explanation: In *Mahender Chawla v. Union of India* (2019), the Supreme Court approved the Witness Protection Scheme and emphasized state protection for vulnerable witnesses.

subject: BSA
question: By which of the following ways under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the credit of a witness MAY be impeached by adverse party?
options: By the evidence of persons who testify that they, from their knowledge of the witness, believe him to be unworthy of credit
By proof that the witness has been bribed, or has accepted the offer of bribe
By proof of former statements inconsistent with any part of his evidence which is liable to be contradicted
explanation: Under Section 158 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 155 of the old Evidence Act), the credit of a witness may be impeached by all three statutory methods.

subject: BSA
question: A witness declaring another witness to be unworthy of credit MAY NOT, upon his examination-in-chief, give reasons for his belief, but he MAY be asked his reasons in cross-examination:-
options: The answers which he gives can be contradicted, if they are false
The answers which he gives cannot be contradicted
The answers which he gives cannot be contradicted, though if they are false, he may afterwards be charged with giving false evidence
explanation: Under Section 158 Explanation to BSA, 2023, answers given in cross-examination regarding reasons for unworthiness cannot be contradicted, though false answers render him liable for perjury.

subject: BSA
question: A photograph can be proved by examination of photographer and by proving the negative. It was held in which case?
options: State of Gujarat vs. Bharat, 1991 Cr.L.J. 978
Purushothama vs. S. Perumal, AIR 1972 SC 608
S.R. Wadekar vs. UOI, AIR 1993 Bom. 64
explanation: In *State of Gujarat v. Bharat* (1991), it was held that proof of a photograph requires examining the photographer and producing the negative.

subject: BSA
question: In the absence of substantive evidence:-
options: corroborative evidence may be or may not be used as per the discretion of the Court
explanation: Corroborative evidence is supplementary evidence; without independent substantive evidence, corroborative evidence alone has no legal value to sustain conviction.

subject: BSA
question: Former statement of a witness MAY be proved to corroborate later testimony as to the same fact, as provided under Section............of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:-
explanation: Section 160 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 157 of the old Evidence Act) governs former statements of witness used to corroborate later testimony as to same fact.

subject: BSA
question: Statement of an injured person is recorded as dying declaration, however he survives. His statement is admissible under which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: If an injured person survives after making a dying declaration, it ceases to be admissible under Section 26, but is admissible under Section 160 BSA to corroborate his testimony in court.

subject: BSA
question: When a person in anticipation of death makes his dying declaration in terms of Section 26, but thereafter survives, in such an eventuality the statement so recorded can be used as a statement under:-
explanation: Under Section 160 BSA for corroboration (or Section 148 BSA for contradiction).

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following is true about First Information Report (FIR)?
options: It is not a substantive evidence
It is an important secondary evidence
explanation: FIR is NOT substantive evidence; it can only be used under Section 160 BSA to corroborate or under Section 148 BSA to contradict the informant.

subject: BSA
question: In relation to F.I.R., which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: It is not a substantive evidence
It merely marks the beginning of the investigation
It cannot be used as a previous statement for any purpose
The informant need not be an eye witness
explanation: Statement C is INCORRECT because FIR CAN be used as a previous statement to corroborate (Section 160 BSA) or contradict (Section 148 BSA) the maker.

subject: BSA
question: FIR is not a substantive evidence, it can be used during trial:-
options: to corroborate and contradict the information both
neither to corroborate nor to contradict the information
explanation: FIR can be used both for corroboration (Section 160 BSA) and contradiction (Section 148 BSA).

subject: BSA
question: First Information Report can be used for:-
explanation: FIR can be used to corroborate the informant who lodged it.

subject: BSA
question: A minor girl attempts to commit suicide after rape with her, the suicide note of the girl in respect of rape is:-
options: Admissible u/s. 26(a) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Admissible u/s 160 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Admissible u/s. 26(f) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Admissible u/s 27 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: If she survives the suicide attempt, the note is admissible under Section 160 BSA to corroborate her testimony.

subject: BSA
question: The question is, whether 'A' was ravished and thereafter murdered? The fact that, without making a complaint, she said that she had been ravished:-
options: Is relevant as a substantive evidence
Is relevant as a secondary evidence
May be relevant under Section 26(a) or 160 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Illustration (j) to Section 6 BSA / Section 26(a) / Section 160 BSA.

subject: BSA
question:
Which one of the following statements is correct?
A "Dying Declaration" made under section 26 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is subject to the control of:-
options: Section 183 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 180 and 181 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 56 and 49 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 161 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Section 161 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 158 of the old Evidence Act) governs what matters may be proved in connection with a proved dying declaration under Section 26.

subject: BSA
question: Under which section, the facts proved under Sections 26 and 27 can be contradicted as per Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: Section 161 of BSA, 2023 allows contradicting or corroborating a statement admitted under Section 26 or 27.

subject: BSA
question: Under which provision a witness CAN refresh his memory?
explanation: Section 162 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 159 of the old Evidence Act) governs Refreshing Memory.

subject: BSA
question: Under which of the following sections of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a witness under examination can "while under examination, refresh his memory by referring to any writing made by himself at the time of the transaction concerning which he is questioned..."?
explanation: Section 162 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Under which of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a witness under examination gets the right to refresh his memory?
explanation: Section 162 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: A witness may while under examination, refresh his memory by referring to any writing made by himself at the time of the transaction or soon afterwards. This provision is provided under:-
explanation: Section 162 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Section 162 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides for:-
options: The credit of a witness may be impeached
Court's power to disallow indecent or scandalous question
To put any question which might be put in cross-examination by party to his own witness
explanation: Witness refreshing memory.

subject: BSA
question: Whether a book-keeper may testify to facts recorded by him in books regularly kept in the course of business, although he has forgotten the particular transactions entered?
options: No, because he has forgotten the particular transactions
No, because it cannot be presumed that he kept the books correctly
Yes, if he knows that the books were correctly kept
Cannot testify to facts recorded by him
explanation: Under Section 163 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 160 of the old Evidence Act: testimony to facts stated in document), a witness may testify to facts although he has no specific recollection of the facts themselves, if he is sure that the facts were correctly recorded.

subject: BSA
question: Statement recorded during investigation under Section 180 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can be used during trial:-
explanation: Under Section 183 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 162 CrPC), police statements can be used ONLY for contradicting the witness.

subject: BSA
question: The following is NOT the example of "Best Evidence Rule":-
explanation: Section 167 (old Section 164 IEA: using document produced under notice) is an evidentiary rule of estoppel/waiver, not an example of the Best Evidence Rule.

subject: BSA
question: When a party refuses to produce a document which he has notice to produce, can he use the document as evidence afterwards?
options: He can use it with the consent of other party
He may use it by order of court
explanation: Under Section 167 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 164 of the old Evidence Act), a party refusing to produce a document after notice cannot afterwards use it as evidence without consent of the other party or order of the Court.

subject: BSA
question: "Judge's power to put question or order production" is given under:-
explanation: Section 168 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 165 of the old Evidence Act) governs Judge's power to put questions or order production.

subject: BSA
question: Judges power to put question or order the production of any document or thing is given in...............of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:-
explanation: Section 168 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Power of the Court to *suo motu* examine any person at any stage is under:-
options: Section 166 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 167 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
Section 169 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
explanation: Section 168 BSA, 2023 (read with Section 348 BNSS, 2023 / Section 311 CrPC).

subject: BSA
question: Court question under Section 168 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 can be put to:-
explanation: Section 168 explicitly states that the Judge may ask any question he pleases, in any form, at any time, of any witness, or of the parties.

subject: BSA
question: Under which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, a Judge is empowered to ask any question relevant or irrelevant to a witness or a party to a suit?
explanation: Section 168 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: By which section of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the Judge is empowered in order to discover or to obtain proper proof of relevant facts, ask any question, in any form, at any time, of any witness, or of the parties, about any fact relevant or irrelevant?
explanation: Section 168 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: In which provision a judge may order to produce a thing?
options: Section 348 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 311 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 168 of BSA, 2023 empowers the Judge to order the production of any document or thing.

subject: BSA
question: To reach at a proper conclusion and for proof of relevant fact, court may ask any question, in any form, at any time to any person or witnesses. This power is conferred to the court under which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita / BSA?
explanation: Section 168 of BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: During trial, the judge is NOT empowered to ask a witness any question, whether during examination-in-chief, cross-examination or in re-examination, since that would amount to the judge favouring one litigant or another. Is this proposition true or false?
options: True. This would compromise the neutrality of the judge.
False. Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 confers almost unfettered power upon a judge to question a witness or a party.
False. Only a judge presiding over a civil trial can do so.
True. A judge must never descent into the 'boxing ring' and must remain a neutral umpire at all times.
explanation: The proposition is false. Section 168 BSA confers wide powers on the Judge to ask any question to discover or obtain proper proof of relevant facts.

subject: BSA
question: Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 empowers the judge:-
options: To allow the party to put questions to own witness
To allow the party to put questions to opponents witness
To put himself questions to a party
To allow re-examination of a witness
explanation: Section 168 empowers the Judge himself to put questions to any witness or party.

subject: BSA
question: Whether a judge can ask question during examination of witness?
options: Judge should sit as a spectator during recording of evidence
explanation: Yes, under Section 168 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: Who may ask question about any irrelevant fact to the witness during the trial?
options: By the person who call the witness in evidence
explanation: Under Section 168 BSA, a Judge may ask any question about any fact relevant or irrelevant.

subject: BSA
question: A Judge in India:-
options: is not empowered to put questions on his own to the witnesses or to the parties
is empowered to put questions on his own to the witnesses or to the parties according to his sweet will
is empowered to put questions on his own to the witnesses or to the parties in order to discover or to obtain proper proof of relevant facts
is not empowered to put questions on his own to the witnesses or to the parties as India follows common law doctrines
explanation: A Judge in India is empowered to ask questions *in order to discover or obtain proper proof of relevant facts* under Section 168 BSA.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following chapters of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 deals with 'Improper Admission and Rejection of Evidence'?
explanation: Chapter XI of the BSA, 2023 ('Of Improper Admission and Rejection of Evidence') comprises Section 169 (corresponding to Chapter XI / Section 167 of the old Evidence Act).

subject: BSA
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 provides that the improper admission or rejection of evidence shall not be ground of itself for a new trial?
explanation: Section 169 of the BSA, 2023 (corresponding to Section 167 of the old Evidence Act) provides that the improper admission or rejection of evidence shall not be ground of itself for a new trial or reversal of any decision.

subject: BSA
question: Which section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, makes the provision that there shall be no new trial on the ground of improper admission or rejection of evidence?
explanation: Section 169 BSA, 2023.

subject: BSA
question: Which of the following Act is/are repealed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 under Section 170?
explanation: Section 170 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Chapter XII: Repeal and Savings) explicitly repeals The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872).
